task: PF-06 Embedded MES gap assessment independent static acceptance

delivery.head: 0a77597f94e38873b67565e0b477e120e72a57f8
delivery.worktree: dirty shared WIP; acceptance made no production source change

independentStaticVerification.method: Read-only source inspection plus deterministic text assertions; no build, test, service startup, browser, network, database, or media execution
confirmed: The reference handshake restricts exact parent origins, creates a browser binding, validates signed assertions, consumes challenges once, rejects replay, hashes stored session tokens, and emits Secure HttpOnly SameSite=None cookies.
The reference endpoints cover challenge, assertion, exchange, session read, renew, and revoke under the api/v1 route prefix.
ConfigurationEmbeddedSourcePrincipalResolver reads configured SourceSessions or a specially pre-authenticated claims principal; it contains no real MES HTTP current-user call.
The deterministic ext_ mapping produces an identifier but does not create an Identity user or permission assignment.
The shared frontend supports only mock/http auth modes; AuthSession requires access token, refresh token, user, and permissions; the guard redirects protected routes when that session is absent.
The SignalR client is currently wired to an accessTokenFactory, with no explicit embedded-cookie bootstrap mode.
Collaboration.EmbeddedHost composes Identity, SystemData, ReferenceData, and Collaboration modules but does not explicitly set Collaboration Identity/SystemData modes.
The normal Collaboration API host explicitly sets both modes to Embedded.

The repository sample inherits net10.0; no net452 or net6.0 adapter project was found. The Framework 4.5.2/.NET 6 statement is an integration boundary and recommendation, not implemented adapter evidence.

materialCorrection.handoffClaim: The handoff says omitted Embedded modes default all directory, step-up, file, and audit ports to HTTP.
materialCorrection.repositoryEvidence: DependencyInjection selects HTTP for Identity directory and step-up unless Identity:Mode is Embedded, but selects in-process SystemDataFilePort and SystemDataAuditPort unless SystemData:Mode is exactly Http.
materialCorrection.correctedConclusion: With both settings omitted, Identity directory and step-up use HTTP; SystemData file and audit use in-process implementations. Explicitly setting both modes remains desirable for an unambiguous reference host, but the stated default behavior is not uniform.

realMesCurrentUserAndSso.reason: No real MES current-user/session API contract or adapter is present. Static SourceSessions are test fixtures and cannot prove production SSO.

frontendEmbeddedAuthBootstrapAndGuard.reason: There is no embedded auth mode or cookie-session adoption contract. The existing protected-route guard requires an access/refresh AuthSession with permissions.

embeddedHostModesAndInProcessDependencie.reason: Program omits explicit modes. Identity directory and step-up therefore select HTTP, while SystemData file and audit remain in-process by default. The handoff must correct this distinction.

mediaCoreReuseWithAdapters.reason: WebRTC/SignalR media APIs and the in-process permission/directory seams exist and are reusable, but the ext_ user must resolve in Identity with current permissions; frontend routing, cookie authentication, directory, permission, SystemData, and step-up topology still require explicit integration.

framework452AndNet6HttpBoundary.reason: Independent-process HTTPS integration is the correct decoupling boundary for Framework 4.5.2 and .NET 6 MES hosts, but no concrete adapter project or real MES contract is present. The current sample targets inherited net10.0.

notVerified: Real MES login session and current-user API request/response contract
Tenant, subject, source-session, security-version, display-name, directory, permission, and step-up field mappings
Whether the MES session cookie may be forwarded or must be exchanged server-side
Actual parent/frame origins, HTTPS certificate trust, reverse-proxy paths, CORS, CSP frame-ancestors, Permissions Policy, and third-party cookie behavior
Built frontend deployment entry and embedded session bootstrap/renew/revoke behavior
Runtime directory and permission evaluation for mapped ext_ users
Cross-tenant rejection, subject switch, revocation propagation, multi-instance persistence, and real MES media BindMedia/KeepAlive
Framework 4.5.2 or .NET 6 adapter compilation and interoperability

verdict.reworkScope: Correct the Identity versus SystemData default-mode statement. Production completion additionally requires implementation and independent validation after real MES contracts and deployment topology are supplied.

scopeBoundary: No production code edit, new implementation, build, test, environment probe, media matrix rerun, service lifecycle action, stage, commit, push, deployment, VS interference, or cloud Docker action was performed.
privacy: Contains no credentials, private configuration values, MES session values, user identifiers, SDP, ICE candidates, IP addresses, or media payloads.
